data.narrative:
Long Wall is a late-stage Defense & Security company that has raised $544M to date, founded by Dan Piemont and Harry O'Hanley, both with prior SpaceX and Morgan Stanley experience. The Defense & Security sector includes 10 comparable companies (2 public: DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS; 8 private including Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, and Saronic), though narrow peer comparables at the same stage and valuation tier remain limited.

Given data constraints, a single applicable valuation method was deployed. Stage-progression analysis applied a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Late Stage advancement to the $544M total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $653M. A peer-median approach was not viable; while 26 same-sector peers exist in the broader Defense & Security universe, fewer than three comparables met tight filters for stage, adjacency, and valuation tier simultaneously, making median multiples unreliable.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $555M (low) to $751M (median $653M), anchored on stage-progression mechanics alone. Key uncertainties include revenue run-rate, profitability trajectory, contract concentration, and regulatory or export licensing risk inherent to defense assets. A narrower range would require either revenue or EBITDA multiples applied to current financial performance—data not provided here. Near-term resolution of comparable transaction data in the narrow defense-tech segment would sharpen the band.
